title: SolarIQ streaming telemetry event
description: One inverter's readings at one simulated instant, as published to solar.telemetry.raw. Frozen shared contract: master specification section 9.1 and docs/data-contracts.md section 2. Bounds here are deliberately at least as strict as Member 2's boundary validation in processing/streaming/validation.py, so anything this schema accepts is accepted downstream.

event_id.description: Unique identifier for this event. Member 2 de-duplicates on it, so it must be stable across producer retries of the same reading.

inverter_id.description: Inverter identifier, unique within its plant.

active_power_kw.description: Instantaneous AC output. Never negative; the event builder also enforces the inverter's nameplate rating as an upper bound, which this schema cannot express because the rating is per asset.

energy_today_kwh.description: Cumulative generation since the start of the simulated day. Integrated from power, never decreasing within a day, reset at the day boundary.

irradiance_wm2.description: Plane-of-array irradiance. Clear-sky peak is 1000 W/m^2; the ceiling matches MAX_PLAUSIBLE_IRRADIANCE_WM2 in Member 2's validator, which allows headroom for cloud-edge enhancement.

module_temp_c.description: PV module temperature. Runs hotter than ambient in sun.

status.description: Operational state. WARNING accompanies degraded output; OFFLINE means the asset reports no generation at all.

availability.description: Event-level availability flag: exactly 0 or 1. Member 2 accepts any value in [0, 1], but the frozen contract specifies a flag, so the producer emits only the two endpoints.

timestamp.description: Event time in UTC, ISO 8601 with a Z suffix and second precision. This is SIMULATED time, not wall-clock time: a simulated day spans a full 24 hours here however few real seconds it is compressed into. Every downstream window depends on that.

simulator_scenario.description: Name of the active demo anomaly, or null during normal operation. DEMO METADATA ONLY. No detection logic may read this field: the pipeline must infer faults from the physical readings, or it proves nothing.
